Solving systems by elimination

Elimination replaces an equation with a combination of equations that has the same solutions. Start with a system whose coefficients and right hand side are known. The shape of the matrix tells you how many equations and unknowns to expect.

2.4.2. More rows than columns#

An extra equation can rule out a solution found from the first two. Check that the proposed solution satisfies every equation before you accept it.

2.4.3. More columns than rows#

A variable with no pivot can remain free when the system is consistent. Choose a value for it, then solve for the pivot variables.

2.4.4. Practice

Use row operations to make the first nonzero entry of each row equal to one. Mark the pivot columns, then substitute your answer into the original equations.
